title: Where the gradients line up
sub: Constrained optima are where no feasible direction improves the objective.

scenarios.name: Equality: tangency

frames.caption: Maximize f = x + y on the unit circle. The dashed line is the level set of f through the current point (grey). Blue is ∇f = (1, 1); orange is ∇g, which points straight out of the circle.

Here the level line crosses the circle. Walking along the circle towards the upper right moves onto higher level lines, so this point can't be the maximum. Equivalently, ∇f has a component along the circle.
Closer. The angle between ∇f and ∇g is shrinking.
Almost tangent. The part of ∇f that points along the circle is what is left of the improving direction.
At (1/√2, 1/√2) the level line just touches the circle without crossing, and the arrows are parallel: ∇f = λ∇g with λ = √2/2. No direction along the circle improves f. That is the Lagrange condition.

legend: constraint and level line of f

frames.caption: Section 7: find the point of the shaded region (inside the disk of radius 2, and below y = 1) closest to the target (3, 2). Level sets of f are circles around the target.
Grow the circle until it first touches the region. Everything inside it is better than anything outside, but none of it is feasible yet.
First contact is at the corner (√3, 1), where both constraints are active. This is the minimizer: the region is convex and so is f.

KKT at the corner: −∇f (blue, the way f decreases) must be a non-negative combination of the active constraints' outward gradients. The orange arrows are λ₁∇g₁ (pointing out of the disk) and then λ₂∇g₂ (pointing up, out of y ≤ 1), placed head to tail: they add up exactly to −∇f, with λ₁ = √3 − 1 ≈ 0.73 and λ₂ = 4 − 2√3 ≈ 0.54: both positive. Descent would mean leaving the region, which is what stationarity with λ ≥ 0 says.
